title: Natural selection works only by accumulating very small modifications

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection works only by accumulating very small modifications

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural selection acts only by preserving and accumulating very small inherited modifications, each profitable to its bearer, and so excludes continued creation of new organisms or large sudden changes of structure.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Natural selection can act only by the preservation and accumulation of infinitesimally small inherited modifications, each profitable to the preserved being

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Natural Selection: its power compared with man’s selection, its power on characters of trifling importance, its power at all ages and on both sexes”. Scope: all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern genetics can test the exclusivity claim and existing cases include both small and large effects. It cannot reconstruct every adaptive transition or cleanly separate initial mutation size from later modification.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For documented adaptive transitions, estimate effect sizes of causal inherited variants and reconstruct whether phenotypic change accumulated through small beneficial steps or large-effect mutations. Recurrent adaptive large-effect changes would refute the exclusive 'infinitesimally small' assertion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The phrase 'infinitesimally small' lacks a unique modern threshold.

Surviving genomic signatures underrepresent old or polygenic adaptations.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Because the wording is exclusive, documented large-effect adaptations and polyploid origins in public genetic and chromosomal databases are directly relevant and do not require a survey of every organism. How small a modification must be before it counts as infinitesimal is contested, which blocks a single decision threshold. The data can challenge the strict exclusion of sudden large change and still leave a gradualist, polygenic reading standing.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile the effect sizes of alleles that have contributed to retained adaptive change, and the frequency of polyploid and other macromutational origins. The strict reading would be confirmed only if preserved adaptations are overwhelmingly built from tiny-effect steps. It would be refuted if large-effect alleles or whole-genome duplications repeatedly constitute the inherited change that is kept.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A large-effect allele can still be followed by a long series of small modifiers.

GWAS and QTL samples are biased toward large effects and toward crops, livestock, and humans.

Infinitesimally small can be read as a population-genetic limit or as a ban on large mutations, and those readings diverge.
